purpose: Current assessment, kept SEPARATE from qaSnapshot.json so that reopening a case never rewrites what was observed on the day it was verified.

findings.headline: The presentation is fixed. The relevance behaviour is not, and no tested filter fixes it.
findings.whatWasVerified: On 2026-10-06 the presentation was checked on the released builds and still holds: a search matching nothing says so, and loosely-related suggestions sit behind an explicit action rather than being presented as answers. That verification is accurate about what it checked, and is kept in the recorded snapshot unchanged.
findings.whatRemainsOpen: The system still returns its five nearest matches however unrelated they are. Nothing in it rejects a result for being too far away.
findings.evidence: Measured against the development website on 2026-11-10, read-only, over an expanded set of 31 labelled queries - 23 that should return suggestions and 8 that should not - built specifically to include the hard cases the first 15-query set missed: British spellings, clinical synonyms, real funder acronyms, and nonsense built from real words. Three candidate filters were measured and all three failed. A check against the words actually present in the archive scored 24 of 31: it withheld six genuinely useful searches - paediatric, tumour, haematology and neoplasm on spelling and synonym grounds, and NIAID and PCORI, which are a real NIH institute and a real funder - while still admitting the nonsense search 'snorfulate biodynamics', because 'biodynamics' is a real word in five archived rows. An absolute distance cutoff and a relative-distance margin both failed to separate relevant from irrelevant queries at all: the two ranges overlap, by 0.0324 and 0.0586 respectively, and the best possible absolute cutoff still keeps five of the eight nonsense searches. The mechanism is now understood: the distance measures how well the archive covers the words used, not whether the search was a good one, so a correctly-spelled British word sits further away than most nonsense.
findings.blockedBy: There is no known filter to build. Every rule measured so far either withholds searches people would legitimately make or admits nonsense, and usually both, so changing the behaviour now would trade a visible problem for a worse and less visible one.
findings.whatWouldCloseIt: Either a method that separates useful from useless searches without withholding real ones - which would have to be measured against this same 31-query set and not against a handful of examples - or a business decision that the current behaviour is acceptable given that suggestions are already labelled as suggestions and kept behind an explicit action.
findings.supersededRecommendation: An earlier revision of this finding, written on 2026-11-10 from the first 15-query measurement, named the corpus-vocabulary check as the recommended fix and said it separated the cases cleanly. The expanded 31-query measurement refuted that, and it is recorded here rather than deleted because the claim was acted on: it is the reason the gate was proposed at all. It must not be implemented.
